author: jjdenhertog
body:
Context & Background:
  This is a Node.js/Next.js project using TypeScript, Docker, and pnpm. The main application syncs
  Spotify playlists to Plex. Currently, many Spotify playlists fail to load due to API
  restrictions, causing the system to fail at apps/web/src/helpers/spotify/getSpotifyData.ts:86
  when getSpotifyPlaylist() returns undefined.

  Current System Architecture:
  - Main app: Next.js web app in apps/web/
  - Sync worker: Background service in apps/sync-worker/
  - Shared packages in packages/ directory
  - Uses pnpm workspaces
  - Production runs in Docker with supervisord
  - Current Spotify integration uses @spotify/web-api-ts-sdk

  Key Files to Understand:
  - apps/web/src/helpers/spotify/getSpotifyData.ts - Main entry point, calls getSpotifyPlaylist
  - apps/web/src/helpers/spotify/getSpotifyPlaylist.ts:58 - Where fallback should be added after
  try/catch
  - packages/shared-types/src/index.ts - Contains GetSpotifyPlaylist interface definition
  - Dockerfile - Main production Docker file
  - apps/web/pages/api/saved-items/index.ts:86 - Where getSpotifyData is called from API

  SpotifyScraper Integration Details:
  - GitHub repo: https://github.com/AliAkhtari78/SpotifyScraper
  - It's a Python library that scrapes Spotify without official API
  - Method: client.get_playlist_info(playlist_url) takes full Spotify URLs
  - Returns dict with keys: name, owner (dict with display_name), track_count, followers (dict with
   total), tracks (array)
  - Each track has: name, artists (array with name), album (dict with name), id

  Implementation Specifications:

  1. New Service Structure (apps/spotify-scraper/):
  apps/spotify-scraper/
  ├── Dockerfile
  ├── docker-compose.yml
  ├── README.md
  ├── requirements.txt
  ├── app.py (Flask/FastAPI server)
  └── spotify_scraper_service.py
  2. API Contract:
    - Endpoint: POST http://localhost:3020/playlist
    - Request: {"url": "https://open.spotify.com/playlist/37i9dQZF1DX0XUsuxWHRQd"}
    - Response: Must match GetSpotifyPlaylist exactly:
  interface GetSpotifyPlaylist {
    type: "spotify-playlist"
    id: string
    title: string
    owner: string
    image: string
    tracks: Array<{
      id: string
      title: string
      artist: string
      album: string
      artists: string[]
    }>
  }
  3. Data Transformation Rules:
    - type: Always "spotify-playlist"
    - id: Extract from URL or use SpotifyScraper result
    - title: Map from SpotifyScraper name
    - owner: Map from SpotifyScraper owner.display_name or use empty string
    - image: Use empty string (SpotifyScraper may not provide)
    - tracks[].id: Use SpotifyScraper track id or generate dummy ID
    - tracks[].title: Map from SpotifyScraper track name
    - tracks[].artist: Use first artist from artists array
    - tracks[].album: Map from SpotifyScraper track album.name
    - tracks[].artists: Map from SpotifyScraper track artists array
  4. Fallback Integration Point:
  In getSpotifyPlaylist.ts, modify the catch block at line 58:
  } catch (_e) {
      // Add SpotifyScraper fallback here
      // Convert playlist ID back to Spotify URL
      // Make HTTP request to localhost:3020/playlist  
      // Transform response to match GetSpotifyPlaylist
      return undefined; // Only if SpotifyScraper also fails
  }
  5. URL Conversion Logic:
  // Convert: "37i9dQZF1DX0XUsuxWHRQd" 
  // To: "https://open.spotify.com/playlist/37i9dQZF1DX0XUsuxWHRQd"
  6. Docker Integration:
    - Update main Dockerfile to include SpotifyScraper service
    - Use supervisord to manage both web app and SpotifyScraper
    - SpotifyScraper should start before main app
    - Environment variable: SPOTIFY_SCRAPER_URL=http://localhost:3020
  7. Error Handling:
    - If SpotifyScraper service is down, fail gracefully
    - Log errors but don't crash main application
    - Return undefined if both Spotify API and SpotifyScraper fail

  Technical Constraints:
  - Must use existing project patterns and conventions
  - No modifications to GetSpotifyPlaylist interface
  - No new configuration options in UI
  - Must work in both development and production Docker environments
  - Use project's existing HTTP client patterns (AxiosRequest helper exists)

Important:
- Make sure to run pnpm type-check and pnpm lint and fix any errors before completing this task
- Never use @vibe-kanban as package name. It should always @spotify-to-plex
- Don't overcomplicate things. Look at the rest of the code to understand what the coding approach is (lean & clean)

This PR updates [typing-extensions](https://pypi.org/project/typing-extensions) from **3.10.0.0** to **4.15.0**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 4.15.0
   ```
   No user-facing changes since 4.15.0rc1.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 4.15.0rc1
   ```
   - Add the `typing_extensions.disjoint_base` decorator, as specified
  in PEP 800. Patch by Jelle Zijlstra.
- Add `typing_extensions.type_repr`, a backport of
  [`annotationlib.type_repr`](https://docs.python.org/3.14/library/annotationlib.html#annotationlib.type_repr),
  introduced in Python 3.14 (CPython PR [124551](https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/124551),
  originally by Jelle Zijlstra). Patch by Semyon Moroz.
- Fix behavior of type params in `typing_extensions.evaluate_forward_ref`. Backport of
  CPython PR [137227](https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/137227) by Jelle Zijlstra.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 4.14.1
   ```
   - Fix usage of `typing_extensions.TypedDict` nested inside other types
  (e.g., `typing.Type[typing_extensions.TypedDict]`). This is not allowed by the
  type system but worked on older versions, so we maintain support.
   ```
   
  
  
  
  
   ### 4.14.0rc1
   ```
   - Drop support for Python 3.8 (including PyPy-3.8). Patch by [Victorien Plot](https://github.com/Viicos).
- Do not attempt to re-export names that have been removed from `typing`,
  anticipating the removal of `typing.no_type_check_decorator` in Python 3.15.
  Patch by Jelle Zijlstra.
- Update `typing_extensions.Format`, `typing_extensions.evaluate_forward_ref`, and
  `typing_extensions.TypedDict` to align
  with changes in Python 3.14. Patches by Jelle Zijlstra.
- Fix tests for Python 3.14 and 3.15. Patches by Jelle Zijlstra.

New features:

- Add support for inline typed dictionaries ([PEP 764](https://peps.python.org/pep-0764/)).
  Patch by [Victorien Plot](https://github.com/Viicos).
- Add `typing_extensions.Reader` and `typing_extensions.Writer`. Patch by
  Sebastian Rittau.
- Add support for sentinels ([PEP 661](https://peps.python.org/pep-0661/)). Patch by
  [Victorien Plot](https://github.com/Viicos).
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 4.13.2
   ```
   - Fix `TypeError` when taking the union of `typing_extensions.TypeAliasType` and a
  `typing.TypeAliasType` on Python 3.12 and 3.13.
  Patch by [Joren Hammudoglu](https://github.com/jorenham).
- Backport from CPython PR [132160](https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/132160)
  to avoid having user arguments shadowed in generated `__new__` by
  `typing_extensions.deprecated`.
  Patch by [Victorien Plot](https://github.com/Viicos).
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 4.13.1
   ```
   Bugfixes:

- Fix regression in 4.13.0 on Python 3.10.2 causing a `TypeError` when using `Concatenate`.
  Patch by [Daraan](https://github.com/Daraan).
- Fix `TypeError` when using `evaluate_forward_ref` on Python 3.10.1-2 and 3.9.8-10.
  Patch by [Daraan](https://github.com/Daraan).
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 4.13.0
   ```
   No user-facing changes since 4.13.0rc1.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 4.13.0rc1
   ```
   New features:

- Add `typing_extensions.TypeForm` from PEP 747. Patch by
  Jelle Zijlstra.
- Add `typing_extensions.get_annotations`, a backport of
  `inspect.get_annotations` that adds features specified
  by PEP 649. Patches by Jelle Zijlstra and Alex Waygood.
- Backport `evaluate_forward_ref` from CPython PR
  [119891](https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/119891) to evaluate `ForwardRef`s.
  Patch by [Daraan](https://github.com/Daraan), backporting a CPython PR by Jelle Zijlstra.

Bugfixes and changed features:

- Update PEP 728 implementation to a newer version of the PEP. Patch by Jelle Zijlstra.
- Copy the coroutine status of functions and methods wrapped
  with `typing_extensions.deprecated`. Patch by Sebastian Rittau.
- Fix bug where `TypeAliasType` instances could be subscripted even
  where they were not generic. Patch by [Daraan](https://github.com/Daraan).
- Fix bug where a subscripted `TypeAliasType` instance did not have all
  attributes of the original `TypeAliasType` instance on older Python versions.
  Patch by [Daraan](https://github.com/Daraan) and Alex Waygood.
- Fix bug where subscripted `TypeAliasType` instances (and some other
  subscripted objects) had wrong parameters if they were directly
  subscripted with an `Unpack` object.
  Patch by [Daraan](https://github.com/Daraan).
- Backport to Python 3.10 the ability to substitute `...` in generic `Callable`
  aliases that have a `Concatenate` special form as their argument.
  Patch by [Daraan](https://github.com/Daraan).
- Extended the `Concatenate` backport for Python 3.8-3.10 to now accept
  `Ellipsis` as an argument. Patch by [Daraan](https://github.com/Daraan).
- Fix backport of `get_type_hints` to reflect Python 3.11+ behavior which does not add
  `Union[..., NoneType]` to annotations that have a `None` default value anymore.
  This fixes wrapping of `Annotated` in an unwanted `Optional` in such cases.
  Patch by [Daraan](https://github.com/Daraan).
- Fix error in subscription of `Unpack` aliases causing nested Unpacks
  to not be resolved correctly. Patch by [Daraan](https://github.com/Daraan).
- Backport CPython PR [124795](https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/124795):
  fix `TypeAliasType` not raising an error on non-tuple inputs for `type_params`.
  Patch by [Daraan](https://github.com/Daraan).
- Fix that lists and `...` could not be used for parameter expressions for `TypeAliasType`
  instances before Python 3.11.
  Patch by [Daraan](https://github.com/Daraan).
- Fix error on Python 3.10 when using `typing.Concatenate` and
  `typing_extensions.Concatenate` together. Patch by [Daraan](https://github.com/Daraan).
- Backport of CPython PR [109544](https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/109544)
  to reflect Python 3.13+ behavior: A value assigned to `__total__` in the class body of a
  `TypedDict` will be overwritten by the `total` argument of the `TypedDict` constructor.
  Patch by [Daraan](https://github.com/Daraan), backporting a CPython PR by Jelle Zijlstra.
- `isinstance(typing_extensions.Unpack[...], TypeVar)` now evaluates to `False` on Python 3.11
  and newer, but remains `True` on versions before 3.11.
  Patch by [Daraan](https://github.com/Daraan).
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 4.12.2
   ```
   - Fix regression in v4.12.0 where specialization of certain
  generics with an overridden `__eq__` method would raise errors.
  Patch by Jelle Zijlstra.
- Fix tests so they pass on 3.13.0b2
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 4.12.1
   ```
   - Preliminary changes for compatibility with the draft implementation
  of PEP 649 in Python 3.14. Patch by Jelle Zijlstra.
- Fix regression in v4.12.0 where nested `Annotated` types would cause
  `TypeError` to be raised if the nested `Annotated` type had unhashable
  metadata. Patch by Alex Waygood.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 4.12.0
   ```
   This release is mostly the same as 4.12.0rc1 but fixes one more
longstanding bug.

- Fix incorrect behaviour of `typing_extensions.ParamSpec` on Python 3.8 and
  3.9 that meant that
  `isinstance(typing_extensions.ParamSpec("P"), typing.TypeVar)` would have a
  different result in some situations depending on whether or not a profiling
  function had been set using `sys.setprofile`. Patch by Alex Waygood.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 4.12.0rc1
   ```
   This release focuses on compatibility with the upcoming release of
Python 3.13. Most changes are related to the implementation of type
parameter defaults (PEP 696).

Thanks to all of the people who contributed patches, especially Alex
Waygood, who did most of the work adapting typing-extensions to the
CPython PEP 696 implementation.

Full changelog:

- Improve the implementation of type parameter defaults (PEP 696)
  - Backport the `typing.NoDefault` sentinel object from Python 3.13.
    TypeVars, ParamSpecs and TypeVarTuples without default values now have
    their `__default__` attribute set to this sentinel value.
  - TypeVars, ParamSpecs and TypeVarTuples now have a `has_default()`

author: sebrandon1
body:
This pull request adds new steps to the `action.yml` workflow to reduce the risk of out-of-memory (OOM) errors during CI runs, specifically targeting CRC/QEMU processes. It introduces swap space creation and OOM killer protection mechanisms, and disables the `swap-storage` option in the disk space freeing step to avoid interference with the new swap setup.

**Memory management improvements:**

* Added a step to create an 8GB swap file on `/mnt` if no swap is active, and increased system swappiness to prefer swap usage, helping to reduce OOM risk during heavy memory usage.
* Disabled the `swap-storage` option in the `jlumbroso/free-disk-space` step to prevent it from deleting the newly created swap file.

**OOM killer protection:**

* Introduced a step to lower the OOM killer score for CRC/QEMU and related processes, making them less likely to be terminated during memory pressure. Includes a lightweight watchdog to periodically re-apply the protection for new/restarted processes.

author: harrisonde
body:
# 🚀 Cache System Implementation
This PR introduces a comprehensive caching system to the Adele framework, providing multi-backend cache support with automatic configuration and scheduled maintenance.
## ✨ Features Added
### 🔄 Multi-Backend Cache Support

- Redis Cache - High-performance distributed caching with connection pooling
- Badger Cache - Embedded key-value store for single-instance applications
- Environment-driven auto-detection and configuration

## ⚙️ Framework Integration

- Added Cache interface to main Adele struct for framework-wide access
- Automatic bootstrap during application startup via BootstrapCache()
- Seamless integration with existing bootstrap flow

## 📊 Cache Interface

- Unified Cache interface with methods: Has(), Get(), Set(), Forget(), Empty(), EmptyByMatch()
- JSON-based serialization for cross-backend compatibility using Encode()/Decode()
- Support for TTL (time-to-live) expiration on cache entries

## 🔧 Configuration & Environment Variables

- Redis: REDIS_HOST, REDIS_PORT, REDIS_MAX_IDLE, REDIS_MAX_ACTIVE_CONNECTIONS, REDIS_TIMEOUT, REDIS_PREFIX
- Badger: Uses {rootPath}/resources/badger for storage
- Cache type detection via CACHE, SESSION_TYPE, QUEUE_TYPE environment variables

## ⏰ Automated Maintenance

- Daily Badger value log garbage collection via cron scheduler
- Automatic cleanup of deleted data to maintain optimal performance
- Configurable GC threshold (70% discard ratio)

## 🧪 Comprehensive Testing

- Unit tests for all cache operations and utility functions
- Integration tests using testcontainers for real Redis instances
- BadgerDB tests with temporary file system setup
- Environment variable detection testing

## 🏗️ Technical Implementation
### Redis Driver

- Connection pooling with configurable idle/active limits
- Pattern-based key matching and bulk operations
- Prefix support for multi-tenant applications

### Badger Driver

- Embedded database with configurable storage path
- Efficient batch operations for bulk key deletion
- Background value log compaction

### JSON Serialization

- Universal Entry type (map[string]interface{}) for cache values
- Forward/backward compatible JSON encoding
- Handles complex nested data structures

## 💻 Usage Example
```go
// Framework automatically configures cache based on environment
if app.Cache != nil {
    // Set with TTL
    app.Cache.Set("user:123", userData, 3600)
    
    // Get value
    user, err := app.Cache.Get("user:123")
    
    // Bulk operations
    app.Cache.EmptyByMatch("user:")
}
```

This implementation provides a solid foundation for caching across the Adele framework while maintaining simplicity and performance. The automatic configuration ensures zero-config operation while still supporting advanced use cases. 🎯

body:
This PR fixes the authentication error `{"code":400,"error_code":"validation_failed","msg":"Unsupported provider: provider is not enabled"}` by replacing OAuth authentication with Supabase's email/password authentication system.

## Problem

The application was attempting to use OAuth authentication with an unsupported provider, causing login failures. The `User.login()` method was being called without parameters, suggesting it was designed for OAuth flows rather than email/password authentication.

## Solution

**Created comprehensive User authentication system:**

- **New User Entity**: Implemented `entities/User.js` with full CRUD operations and authentication methods
- **Email/Password Login**: Replaced OAuth with `supabase.auth.signInWithPassword({ email, password })`
- **Proper Error Handling**: Authentication failures throw descriptive errors, successful logins return user objects
- **Form Validation**: Validates email and password presence before attempting authentication

**Updated UI for email/password collection:**

The login flow now presents a user-friendly form instead of OAuth buttons:

1. **Initial state**: Single LOGIN button

    throw new Error('Email and password are required');

  const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.signInWithPassword({

  return new User(userProfile);
}

This pull request introduces a comprehensive implementation of variable expansion (expander) in the `minishell` project, including both code and supporting infrastructure. It adds new expander source files, updates lexer/token structures to track quoting context, and integrates expansion logic into the lexer pipeline. Additionally, it removes some VSCode configuration files and test data.

**Key changes:**

### Expander Implementation

* Added a full set of expander source files: `expander.c`, `expander_utils.c`, `expander_write.c`, `expander_status.c`, `expander_tokens.c`, and `expander_check.c`, implementing variable expansion logic, utility functions, and two-pass expansion for shell variables. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-311c406e1a142b8d1e8b6e3bc7bfef32b68470eb116ed925ff7cb0067165a911R47-R52) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-f3990dcb930218191f6890d1063faa5348a95ac237687308603c6852f61b060eR1-R127) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-d889d33b5bfe137907bb613b8c8644433c63768a1472618f25045bf745437b35R1-R61) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-a2a81b31108ad16ccd8c0ed9491625838b2cfc2c55630c8089394271a61fcc68R1-R129) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-2516604b200848bb8e85f8b30978dbffd0b165e0f5f4917096c5f8603dcc0fa4R1-R103) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-f8427e2973098a5288f5b1f0fc01a1a5124179e3a6cb436c58ab6c53b9b86a7cR1-R33) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-84182128afc7d5e26f446d39570fb9c08ef964c8af095f2d99806547eb15b44fR1-R139)
* Updated the `Makefile` to include these new expander source files in the build process.

### Lexer and Token Structure Updates

* Introduced a new `t_kind` enum to track whether a token is plain, double-quoted, or single-quoted, and added a `kind` field to the `t_lexer` struct.

author: google-labs-jules[bot]
body:
This commit addresses critical stability issues for multi-tenancy.

**Fixes:**
1.  **`UnicodeEncodeError`:** Replaced all standard `print()` calls with `sys.stdout.buffer.write(str.encode('utf-8', 'backslashreplace'))`. This prevents crashes when logging messages or bot responses containing non-ASCII characters, a common issue on Windows environments.
2.  **Interleaved Console Logs:** Introduced a global `logging_lock` that is used for every single write to `stdout`. This synchronizes output from all threads (FastAPI workers, vendor listeners, etc.), ensuring that log messages are printed atomically and are not garbled.

**Affected Files:**
- **`logging_lock.py` (New):** Provides the global lock.
- **`main.py`:** All `print` calls updated.
- **`chatbot_manager.py`:** All `print` calls updated; added a `try/except` block to the message callback for robust error handling.
- **`vendor/whatsAppBaileyes.py`:** All `print` and `sys.stdout.buffer.write` calls updated to use the lock and safe encoding.
- **`queue_manager.py`:** Replaced its own internal lock with the new global lock and updated all `sys.stdout.buffer.write` calls to be thread-safe.

author: vpollo11
body:
### Fix ambiguous instruction about row indexing

#### What changed

The sentence:

> "Load the data using genfromtxt, specifying the delimiter as ';', and optimize the numpy array size by reducing the data types. Use np.float32 and verify that the resulting numpy array weighs 76800 bytes."

was unclear about whether the CSV header should be skipped or not.

It now says:

> "Load the data using genfromtxt, specifying the delimiter as ';' with excluding the headers, and optimize the numpy array size by reducing the data types. Use np.float32 and verify that the resulting numpy array weighs 76800 bytes."

#### Why

Later instructions refer to specific row numbers (like the 2nd, 7th, and 12th rows). Without stating whether the header counts as a row, the meaning is ambiguous — it affects the indexing. This fix makes it clear that the header should be excluded.

#### No code changes

This is a documentation fix only.

body:
# What does this PR do?

We have two separate sources of events: the regular API events and the Prometheus events, so we have two causes of drifts.

Regular events: we force the events to align with  the chart datapoints, but this is done by creating an "alignTimestamp" which is not really accurate. I removed this "grid snapping" logic but if we want to keep it anyway we need to find a better solution as it is likely the source of our problem.

Prometheus events: zooming in affects dynamicRange, which is then used by Prometheus to fetch the data, causing a drift:   k8s_event_logger_q_k8s_events_total{...} offset ${dynamicRange}. I've added timerange caching and instant query to fix this. No more drifting.

author: brynary
body:
Hello and thank you for SimpleCov!

This PR updates the detection for the `CC_TEST_REPORTER_ID` environment variable to also detect the `QLTY_COVERAGE_TOKEN` env var.

Context: As of this year, the Code Climate Quality product has been replaced by the newer [Qlty Cloud](https://qlty.sh/) edition. (Qlty Cloud is operated by the same team previously responsible for Code Climate Quality.)

Qlty Cloud uses the `QLTY_COVERAGE_TOKEN` env var in the same way that Code Climate Quality used `CC_TEST_REPORTER_ID`. This PR ensures JSON code coverage data is automatically generated when it is present.

We discovered that some customers are not aware of the `CC_TEST_REPORTER_ID` behavior and when they switched from `CC_TEST_REPORTER_ID` to `QLTY_COVERAGE_TOKEN` it was confusing that the JSON went missing.

This PR also preserves the `CC_TEST_REPORTER_ID` behavior for backwards compatibility, for anyone where it may be a "load bearing" behavior.

Please let me know if you have any questions about this change!

-Bryan

author: parth-07
body:
This commit fixes fragment padding size computation when output section address is unaligned. The fragment padding size computation (incorrectly) assumed that the fragment offset is congruent to the output section address (modulo fragment alignment). This assumption is violated when the output section address is explicitly specified in the linker script.

This change is causing UnalignedCrash.test to fail because the test expects the link to fail but now the link is passing. The link passing seems correct as both bfd/lld pass as well for this test case.

Resolves #346

This PR addresses the requirement to add visualization capabilities for viewing database entries and exits via CLI. While the system already had complete insertion routines (`entrada-unica`, `entrada-lotes`, `saida-unica`, `saida-lotes`), it was missing the ability to query and display this data.

## Changes Made

### Repository Layer
- Added `fetch_all()` and `fetch_by_filters()` methods to `EntradaRepo` class
- Added `fetch_all()` and `fetch_by_filters()` methods to `SaidaRepo` class
- Both methods support optional filtering by product code, date range, and result limiting

### CLI Commands
Added a new `consultar` subcommand group with two commands:

```bash
# List all entries with optional filters
python -m estoque.adapters.cli consultar entradas [--codigo CODE] [--data-inicio DATE] [--data-fim DATE] [--limite N]

# List all exits with optional filters  
python -m estoque.adapters.cli consultar saidas [--codigo CODE] [--data-inicio DATE] [--data-fim DATE] [--limite N]
```

### Features
- **Rich table formatting**: Uses existing `_display_table()` for consistent UI
- **Flexible filtering**: Filter by product code, date ranges, or limit results
- **User-friendly output**: Shows "no records found" message when filters return empty results
- **Portuguese interface**: Commands and help text in Portuguese to match existing CLI

## Example Usage

```bash
# View recent entries
$ python -m estoque.adapters.cli consultar entradas --limite 10

# Filter entries by product code
$ python -m estoque.adapters.cli consultar entradas --codigo TEST003

# View exits within a date range
$ python -m estoque.adapters.cli consultar saidas --data-inicio 2025-01-01 --data-fim 2025-01-31
```

## Testing
- All existing tests pass without modification
- New repository methods tested via CLI integration
- Backward compatibility maintained for all existing functionality

This completes the database visualization requirements while maintaining the existing insertion capabilities and following the established CLI patterns and styling.

## 🎯 Overview

The AI governance bundle introduces automated workflows, policy enforcement, metrics collection, and comprehensive documentation to ensure responsible AI assistance while maintaining code quality and security standards.

## 🔧 Core Components

### Configuration & Workflows
- **`.claude.yml`** - Central AI configuration defining review modes, diff thresholds, security flags, and governance controls

- All actions require explicit human authorization for sensitive operations

### Data Governance

- Access controls aligned with repository permissions

- **Ethical Harmonics**: All AI actions filtered through sovereignty principles

BEGINRELEASENOTES
- Allow to pass multiple old datamodel schemas to `podio_class_generator.py`

ENDRELEASENOTES

Fixes #796 

- [x] Includes #803 
- [x] Includes #844 
- [x] Includes #845 
- [x] Includes #886 
- [x] Includes #817 
- [x] Actual tests with multiple schema definitions

This PR adds the possibility to pass multiple old datamodel versions to the datmodel generator and adds tests using two old versions. With these changes it should now be possible to pass an arbitrary number of old schemas to the code generator and validate that each evolution from the old version to the current version is possible (otherwise there will be no code generation).

To achieve this **the grammar for the evolution files had to be changed to accommodate for the possibility of describing all possible schema jumps in one evolution file**. 

Compared to #817 the cmake functionality was slightly adapted to accept multiple old datamodel versions and to allow to write to multiple (i.e. exactly two) old versions and reading those files back from one source file.

- [x] Release notes

author: copilot
body:
## Problem

Google's Rich Results Test was returning no results for the DT Visuals website because the site lacked structured data (JSON-LD schema markup). While the site had good basic SEO with meta tags, Open Graph, and Twitter cards, it was missing the structured data that Google uses to generate rich search results.

## Solution

This PR implements comprehensive structured data using JSON-LD schema markup to enable Google Rich Results for the DT Visuals video production website. The implementation includes both static and dynamic structured data generation.

### Static Structured Data (HTML Head)

Added two main JSON-LD schemas directly to `client/index.html`:

1. **LocalBusiness Schema** - Complete business information including:
   - Company details (name, description, URL)
   - Geographic location (Leicestershire, UK with coordinates)
   - Service catalog with 4 video production offerings
   - Contact point structure for customer service

2. **FAQ Schema** - Structured Q&A data covering:
   - Service types and offerings
   - Geographic coverage and location
   - Monthly retainer partnerships
   - Cinematic production approach

### Dynamic Structured Data System

Created a flexible system for page-specific structured data:

- **`structured-data-utils.ts`** - Utility functions for generating various schema types (Organization, VideoObject, BreadcrumbList, Services)
- **`use-structured-data.tsx`** - React hook that dynamically injects/removes structured data based on page context
- **Dynamic schemas** - BreadcrumbList for navigation, VideoObject for featured content, and enhanced Organization data with dynamic contact information

### Enhanced SEO Meta Tags

Improved existing meta tags with:
- Business-specific Open Graph properties
- Geographic location data (coordinates, region, locale)
- Enhanced robot directives and googlebot instructions
- UK locale specification (en_GB)

## Rich Results Enabled

This implementation enables the following Google Rich Results:

- **Business Information** - Company name, location, services, and contact details
- **Service Listings** - Professional video production service descriptions
- **FAQ Snippets** - Expandable Q&A results in search
- **Local Business Results** - Geographic optimization for UK searches
- **Navigation Breadcrumbs** - Dynamic page navigation structure
- **Video Content** - Rich results for featured video content

## SEO Keywords Targeted

The structured data specifically targets these high-value keywords from the SEO strategy:
- video production company UK
- luxury event videographer
- corporate video production UK
- music video production UK
- monthly video production retainer
- Leicestershire video production

## Validation

Included a validation script (`validate-structured-data.js`) that confirms:
- All JSON-LD syntax is valid
- Required schema properties are present
- Meta tag coverage is complete
- Geographic data is properly formatted

The validation shows 2/2 schemas are valid and Rich Results are now enabled.

## Testing

To test the implementation:
1. Visit [Google Rich Results Test](https://search.google.com/test/rich-results)
2. Enter URL: https://dt-visuals.com
3. Verify LocalBusiness and FAQPage rich results are detected
4. Monitor performance in Google Search Console

This resolves the original issue where Google's Rich Results Test found no structured data, and provides a solid foundation for improved search visibility and rich results display.

author: milagrosmarin
body:
# element-moseq v1.0.0: Major Refactor with Breaking Changes

This pull request delivers a comprehensive refactor of the `element-moseq` project, focusing on environment management, configuration handling, and pipeline enhancements. Most notably, the code is updated to work with the latest version of `keypoint-moseq`, introduces new features that are incompatible with previous `element-moseq` versions, and modernizes the development and packaging setup.

## Breaking Changes

- **`keypoint-moseq` updated** from pinned `0.4.8` to the latest upstream version (installed from source)
- Introduces **five major breaking changes** that are not backward-compatible with earlier `element-moseq` versions:
  - Rename `kpms_reader` functions to generate, load, and update kpms config files
  - Rename `PCAPrep` to `PreProcessing` table and add new attributes
  - Add feature to remove outlier keypoints in `PreProcessing` table with new `outlier_scale_factor` attribute in `PCATask` (only available in latest version of kpms)
  - Add `sigmasq_loc` feature in `PreFit` and `FullFit` to automatically estimate sigmasq_loc (prior controlling the centroid movement across frames) (only available in latest version of kpms)
  - Refactor `PreProcessing` table to use 3-part make function with new `Video` part table

These changes require database and pipeline alignment with the latest `keypoint-moseq` conventions.

## New Features

- **New `report` schema** with comprehensive reporting capabilities
- **New `plotting` module** with refactored `viz_utils` for better organization
- **Enhanced `PreProcessing` table** with 3-part make function, new `Video` part table, and attributes `video_duration`, `frame_rate`, and `average_frame_rate`
- **Support for both DLC config file extensions** (`config.yml` and `config.yaml`)
- **Updated model naming and folder structure** with improved varchar lengths and primary attribute-based naming

## Environment & Packaging Modernization

- Migrated from `setup.py` → `pyproject.toml` and `conda_env.yml`, aligning with modern Python packaging standards
- Simplified and consolidated environment definitions for easier reproducibility
- Updated devcontainer to Python 3.11 and upgraded dependencies
- Removed JAX dependencies from `pyproject.toml`
- Updated pre-commit hooks for improved linting and consistency

## Configuration & Path Handling

- Fixed config functions with proper renaming to match `keypoint-moseq` logic
- Updated all usages (e.g., in `moseq_infer.py`, `moseq_train.py`, `report.py`) to ensure consistent, maintainable DataJoint config handling
- Improved path and directory handling using `Path` objects and robust existence checks
- Refactored `moseq_infer` paths and applied 3-part make function
- Updated folder naming logic to use string of combined primary attributes instead of datetime in `PreFit` and `FullFit`

## Bug Fixes & Improvements

- Removed redundancy of variables in `PreProcessing` table
- Fixed deprecated datetime usage
- Fixed filename generation in `Inference` table
- Bugfix in `Model` imported foreign key
- Updated tutorial pipeline and documentation
- Enhanced docstrings across all modules
- Updated pipeline images to reflect new architecture

## Impact Summary

- **135 total commits** since August 2024
- **42 significant commits** with features, fixes, and refactoring
- **5 breaking changes** requiring user attention
- **Major version bump** from 0.3.2 to 1.0.0 due to breaking changes

author: octoaide[bot]
body:
This pull request addresses issue #1201 by migrating the `aicers/giganto` project from `bincode` version 1 to version 2.

The transition to `bincode` v2 introduces significant API changes, particularly for serialization and deserialization, as well as error handling. This migration updates the codebase to be compatible with the new `bincode` v2 APIs while ensuring backward compatibility where necessary.

### Key Changes Made:

1.  **Updated Cargo.toml dependency**: Changed `bincode = "1"` to `bincode = { version = "2", features = ["serde"] }`.
2.  **Migrated `serialize` calls**: Replaced `bincode::serialize(&data)` with `bincode::serde::encode_to_vec(&data, bincode::config::legacy())` across 91 instances.
3.  **Migrated `deserialize` calls**: Replaced `bincode::deserialize::<T>(&data)` with `bincode::serde::decode_from_slice::<T, _>(&data, bincode::config::legacy())?.0` across 65+ instances.
4.  **Error Handling**: Adapted code for the removal of `bincode::Error` enum, maintaining existing error handling patterns like `.unwrap()`, `?`, and `.map_err()`. All code using the former `bincode::Error` type has been updated to handle the new `EncodeError` and `DecodeError` where applicable.
5.  **Backward Compatibility**: Utilized `bincode::config::legacy()` to ensure data format compatibility with existing serialized data.
6.  **Compilation Fixes**: Addressed tuple access patterns for the new API return types (which now return `(value, bytes_read)`), missing configuration parameters, and type inference issues.

### Quality Assurance:

*   All existing tests pass (156 + 157 tests, 0 failures).
*   Code compiles cleanly without warnings or errors.
*   Clippy checks pass with no issues.

Closes #1201

body:
This pull request introduces a comprehensive framework for measuring and analyzing gas consumption when interacting with CosmWasm vault contracts via EVM precompiles. The changes include a new Solidity interface for vault deposit testing, Go helpers for WASM contract deployment and initialization, detailed gas consumption test suites, and extensive debug logging in the WASM precompile implementation. These improvements enable precise benchmarking and comparison of gas costs across direct WASM calls, EVM precompile calls, and complex multi-operation scenarios.

### Vault Gas Measurement Interface and Documentation

* Added `SimpleVaultInterface.sol`, a simplified Solidity contract for vault deposit flows and gas measurement, including ERC20-to-bank token conversion and vault deposit functionality.
* Added `VAULT_GAS_README.md` to document the test setup, measurement points, and key findings for vault gas consumption benchmarking.

### WASM Contract Deployment and Initialization

* Implemented `SetupVaultContracts` in `export.go` to automate deployment and initialization of vault-related WASM contracts, including vault and token minter contracts, for gas testing scenarios.

### Gas Consumption Test Suite

* Added `wasm_gas_test.go`, a suite of Go tests to measure and compare gas consumption for direct WASM calls, EVM precompile interactions, and multi-operation executions, with summary and benchmarking outputs.

### Debug Logging for WASM Precompile

* Enhanced `wasm.go` with detailed debug logs at key stages: initial gas, method invocation, gas consumed per method, before/after WASM execution and query, and final gas charging to EVM contracts, to facilitate granular analysis of gas usage and overhead. As mentioned in #61136 the auto generated php configs assumes ArrayNode's are by default lists.

The workflow component docs for example show defining metadata with a key value array

 $pullRequest->place()

author: nishantbansal2003
body:
Fixes: #49 

When a fuzz target experiences a crash, the failing inputs are placed in the `testdata/fuzz` directory. If another fuzz target from the same package is running in parallel, it may encounter a false crash due to these shared failing inputs.

To fix this, I created separate binaries for each fuzz target and placed them in the `BinaryDir/<pkg>/<target>/` folder. These binaries are then used to run fuzzing inside Docker, which ensures isolation whenever a fuzz crash occurs.

body:
## 🎯 Summary

This PR represents a major documentation overhaul that repositions LionAGI as an **orchestration engine** rather than an operation library. The key philosophy: **"You bring the operations, we provide the orchestration engine."**

## 🔄 Key Changes

### Philosophy & Messaging
- ✨ Introduced "orchestration engine" concept throughout documentation
- 📚 Created comprehensive philosophy document explaining the paradigm shift
- 🎯 Updated all core concepts to reflect minimal Branch interface (`chat`, `communicate`, `operate`, `react`)

### Bug Fixes & Improvements
- 🔗 Fixed broken GitHub links (master → main branch)
- 🧹 Removed 100+ auto-appended abbreviations cluttering every page
- ❌ Removed intrusive "Was this page helpful?" widget
- 📝 Fixed all markdown formatting issues (trailing backslashes)
- 🎨 Added custom CSS for improved readability and spacing

### New Documentation
- **`lionagi-philosophy.md`**: Explains the evolution from operation library to orchestration engine
- **`orchestration-first.md`**: Quick start guide with new mindset
- **`docs/tests/`**: Testing infrastructure for documentation code examples

### Structural Improvements
- 🏗️ Reorganized navigation: Philosophy → Core Concepts → Patterns
- 📊 Simplified sidebar for better user experience
- 💫 Visual improvements with custom styling

## 📖 Core Message

LionAGI is evolving from v0.x (collection of operations) to v1.0+ (orchestration engine):

**Before:**
```python
# Branch bloated with dozens of operations
branch.analyze()
branch.plan()
branch.summarize()
# ... many more built-in operations
```

**After:**
```python
# Branch as minimal interface
branch.chat()        # Basic LLM interaction
branch.communicate() # Structured communication
branch.operate()     # Execute ANY operation
branch.react()       # ReAct pattern

# Everything else is user-defined
my_op = create_operation(...)
await branch.operate(my_op)
```

## 🧪 Testing

- Created test infrastructure in `docs/tests/` for validating code examples
- All documentation examples updated to match actual API
- Custom CSS tested for light/dark theme compatibility

## 📚 Documentation Impact

This PR affects how users understand and approach LionAGI:
- Shifts mindset from "what operations does LionAGI provide?" to "what do I want to orchestrate?"
- Emphasizes composition and flexibility over fixed functionality
- Positions LionAGI as framework-agnostic orchestration layer

## ✅ Checklist

- [x] Documentation follows project standards
- [x] All markdown properly formatted
- [x] Navigation structure improved
- [x] Code examples updated for accuracy
- [x] Custom styling enhances readability
- [x] Philosophy clearly communicated

author: michaeldmurphy1
body:
## Proposed changes

<!--
At a high level, describe what this PR does.
-->

This adds more infrastructure around cartoon_partial_derivatives().
1. It creates the singular partial functions that some evolution systems requires (takes tensor, not Variables), i.e. `cartoon_partial_derivative()`.
2. Creates a wrapper function called `partial_derivatives()` which takes an extra parameter, the inertial coordinates, and at runtime calls either normal partial derivatives or cartoon partials based on mesh bases.
3. Modifies `DerivCompute` to potentially call the `partial_derivatives()` function with inertial coords that in turn calls the calls the appropriate partial function.

*Note*: I couldn't keep just one structure with an optional parameter (`inertial_coords`) for `DerivCompute` because I can't have two static constexpr `function` pointer members and using brigand won't help because the parameter signature changes (either with or without `inertial_coords`)

author: cvazquezbr
body:
This commit addresses a persistent and complex bug where text in HTML fields would not wrap correctly in the final generated image. It also reverts a previous change that broke the live preview.

1.  **Revert `FieldPositioner.jsx`**: The component is restored to its original state, fixing a regression that broke the live preview's responsive font scaling.

2.  **Replace `html2canvas` with SVG `foreignObject`**: The root cause of the text wrapping issue was the unreliable nature of `html2canvas` for rendering off-screen DOM elements. The `renderHtmlToCanvas` function in `src/utils/htmlRenderer.js` has been completely rewritten to use the more robust and reliable SVG `foreignObject` technique. This method embeds the styled HTML within an SVG, which is then drawn to the canvas as an image, ensuring that text wrapping, padding, and all other CSS properties are rendered exactly as they would be by the browser.

body: # Overview/summary ## This PR fixes/adds/changes/removes 1. fixes #473 ### Breaking changes 1. Removes the resource group and lock provisioning capability from the virtual network and user assigned identity submodules. 2. Changed the network security group, route table, and user assigned identity submodules to use `parent_id` instead of subscription id and resource group name. 3. For the virtual network, network security group, route table, and user assigned identity sub modules added the following keys, where one must be provided: `resource_group_key` and `resource_group_name_existing`. ## Testing evidence Please provide testing evidence to show that your Pull Request works/fixes as described and documented above. - Added setup functions to provision resource groups for deploy tests for usermanagedidentity and virtualnetwork. - Performed an upgrade in lab environment. ### Lab Testing 1. Run the subscription vending automation and reproduce the Resource Group not found error using v5.2.0 2. Run the subscription vending automation without route table or network security groups using v5.2.0 3. Enable route table and network security groups using v5.2.0 4. Update the repo to use new feature branch with bug fix and refactoring 5. Identified a situation where the moved blocks are not succeeding due to an ambiguous body error and fixed within this branch. 6. Perform migration and verify no resource would be replaced or deleted. ## Migration Guidance This migration guidance is for users that were leveraging the resource group and resource group lock creation option within the virtual network and user assigned identity submodules. If you were already using the resource group module to provision all resource groups, no migration steps are required. Migration steps 4-5 apply to updates required for your route table and network security group objects. 1. Change the **terraform-azurerm-lz-vending** version to `6.0.0`. 2. Add new resource group objects to the `resource_groups` map and set the root module variable `resource_group_creation_enabled` to `true`. 3. Remove the `resource_group_creation_enabled`, `resource_group_name`, `resource_group_lock_enabled`, and `resource_group_lock_name` attributes from your virtual networks and user managed identity objects. 4. For virtual networks, user managed identities, route tables and network security groups, change the `resource_group_name` attribute to `resource_group_key` and change the value to the key name that corresponds to the object in the `resource_groups` map. This is to maintain consistency throughout the submodules. 5. If you do not wish to manage the resource group creation with this module at all, then you may specify the `resource_group_name_existing` attribute instead to leverage an already existing resource group within the subscription. This module first checks for the `resource_group_key` and then the `resource_group_name_existing` as a fallback. 6. Add Terraform moved blocks for your resource group and resource group locks as shown below. ```hcl # VNET moved { from = module.lz_vending.module.virtualnetwork[0].azapi_resource.rg[""] to = module.lz_vending.module.resourcegroup[""].azapi_resource.rg } # VNET LOCK moved { from = module.lz_vending.module.virtualnetwork[0].azapi_resource.rg_lock[""] to = module.lz_vending.module.resourcegroup[""].azapi_resource.rg_lock[0] } # UMI moved { from = module.lz_vending.module.usermanagedidentity[""].azapi_resource.rg[0] to = module.lz_vending.module.resourcegroup[""].azapi_resource.rg } # UMI LOCK moved { from = module.lz_vending.module.usermanagedidentity[""].azapi_resource.rg_lock[0] to = module.lz_vending.module.resourcegroup[""].azapi_resource.rg_lock[0] } ``` ## As part of this pull request I have - [x] Checked for duplicate [Pull Requests](https://github.com/Azure/terraform-azurerm-lz-vending/pulls) - [x] Associated it with relevant [issues](https://github.com/Azure/terraform-azurerm-lz-vending/issues), for tracking and closure. - [x] Run and `make fmt` & `make docs` to format your code and update documentation. - [x] Created unit and deployment tests and provided evidence. - [x] Updated relevant and associated documentation.

author: subtlegradient
body:
This pull request significantly improves the documentation, type exports, and developer experience for the `@effect-native/bun-test` package. The main focus is to provide clearer, more comprehensive guides and API documentation for users, as well as to enhance TypeScript integration and update package metadata for consistency.

**Key improvements include:**

### Documentation and Usage Guides

* Completely rewrote and expanded the `README.md` to provide detailed explanations, real-world examples, and advanced usage patterns (including time control, property-based testing, resource management with layers, and flaky test retries). This makes it much easier for users to understand and effectively use the library.

### TypeScript API and Developer Experience

* Changed `export * from "bun:test"` to `export type * from "bun:test"` in `src/index.ts`, ensuring only types (not runtime values) are re-exported, which improves TypeScript compatibility and avoids conflicts.
* Added detailed JSDoc comments and usage examples to all main types and interfaces in `src/index.ts`, making the API much more discoverable and IDE-friendly. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-7d933a882a2353b1c049de301164e25d3f04429cebbd6182e33adbe9e1361b45R80-R200) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-7d933a882a2353b1c049de301164e25d3f04429cebbd6182e33adbe9e1361b45R221-R314) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-7d933a882a2353b1c049de301164e25d3f04429cebbd6182e33adbe9e1361b45R323-R335) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-7d933a882a2353b1c049de301164e25d3f04429cebbd6182e33adbe9e1361b45R354-R461)
* Re-exported all core Bun test runner methods (e.g., `describe`, `it`, `expect`, etc.) for easier access and improved ergonomics.

### Package Metadata and Peer Dependencies

* Updated `package.json` metadata to use the correct repository URLs and descriptions, aligning with the new GitHub organization and project naming.
* Added `@types/bun` as a peer dependency to ensure consumers get proper type support for Bun APIs.

These changes make the library much more approachable for new users and more powerful for advanced users, while also improving TypeScript support and package consistency.

author: pastapastapasta
body:
This commit fixes multiple critical bugs related to height handling when syncing from a checkpoint:

1. Storage Layer Issues (dash-spv/src/storage/disk.rs):
   - Fixed store_headers_from_height to use storage indices instead of blockchain heights for segment calculation
   - Added sync_base_height tracking to properly convert between blockchain and storage heights
   - Fixed filter header storage to track blockchain heights while using storage indices internally
   - Updated index rebuilding to account for checkpoint sync

2. Filter Sync Issues (dash-spv/src/sync/filters.rs):
   - Added blockchain_to_storage_height and storage_to_blockchain_height helper methods
   - Fixed all get_header() calls to convert blockchain heights to storage indices first
   - Added special handling to store checkpoint filter header for chain verification
   - Fixed verify_filter_header_chain to skip verification for first batch after checkpoint

3. Height Double-Counting Issues:
   - Fixed sequential sync manager to not add sync_base_height to already-absolute filter tip heights
   - Fixed status display to use filter tip height directly without offset

These changes ensure proper synchronization when starting from a checkpoint (e.g., height 1,100,000) by correctly handling the distinction between absolute blockchain heights and relative storage indices.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)

## Description

This MR introduces the complete MVEC Relay Control Library - a comprehensive C++ library for controlling and monitoring MVEC (Multi-Vehicular Electronic Controller) devices over J1939 CAN bus. The library provides both synchronous and asynchronous interfaces for relay control, status monitoring, and device management with robust error handling and thread-safe operations.

This is a foundational library that will enable integration with MVEC hardware devices for relay control in robotic and industrial automation systems.

## Highlighted Changes

**mvec_lib/include/mvec_lib/mvec_relay_socketcan.hpp**
- High-level asynchronous interface with thread-safe promise/future patterns
- Non-blocking relay commands and queries with timeout support  
- Optional getters for status messages with automatic validation

**mvec_lib/src/mvec_relay.cpp**
- Core J1939 message parsing and relay command generation
- Bit-level data packing for efficient CAN frame serialization
- Support for relay control, population queries, and diagnostic monitoring

**mvec_lib/include/mvec_lib/core/mvec_constants.hpp**
- Complete J1939 protocol constants and message structure definitions
- Hardware limits and value constraints for MVEC devices
- Comprehensive message type enumeration

**mvec_lib/test/test_mvec_socketcan_hardware.cpp**
- Hardware integration tests with real CAN bus communication
- Population queries, relay state validation, and automatic status monitoring
- Conditional compilation based on CAN_AVAILABLE environment variable

author: copilot
body:
## Problem

The `/api/logs` endpoint was querying columns that don't exist in the actual `admin_logs` database schema, causing 500 errors once authorization issues are resolved. The current implementation queries `(actor_id, resource, metadata, created_at)` while the migration defines `(id, timestamp, admin, action, details)`.

Additionally, the admin UI expects certain query parameters for backward compatibility that weren't supported.

## Solution

### Schema Compatibility Fix
Updated the SQL query to match the actual `admin_logs` table schema:

**Before:**
```sql
SELECT id, actor_id, action, resource, metadata, created_at
FROM admin_logs
ORDER BY created_at DESC
```

**After:**
```sql
SELECT id, timestamp, admin, action, details
FROM admin_logs
ORDER BY timestamp {order_dir}
```

### Backward Compatibility Features
Added support for admin UI query parameters:

1. **`page_size` parameter**: Acts as alias for `limit` with priority for backward compatibility
2. **`sort` parameter**: Supports `-timestamp` (DESC, default) and `timestamp` (ASC) for flexible ordering

### Enhanced Documentation
- Updated function docstrings to reflect correct schema and new parameters
- Comprehensive README.md update with:
  - Environment requirements (`SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY` for RLS bypass)
  - Complete API documentation with examples
  - Deployment and validation instructions

## API Changes

The endpoint responses now correctly return:
```json
{
  "data": [
    { "id": "...", "timestamp": "...", "admin": "...", "action": "...", "details": "..." }
  ],
  "pagination": { "page": 1, "per_page": 50, "total": 123 }
}
```

Query parameters supported:
- `page`: int (default 1)
- `limit` | `page_size`: int (default 50, max 200, page_size takes priority)
- `sort`: `"-timestamp"` (DESC, default) or `"timestamp"` (ASC)

## Testing

- ✅ Python syntax validation passed
- ✅ Flask app imports successfully with changes
- ✅ Blueprint registration confirmed
- ✅ Schema columns verified against migration
- ✅ All requirements implemented and validated

The health endpoint `/api/logs/health` remains unchanged and continues to require admin authentication.

## Deployment Notes

After merging, ensure:
1. Database migration is applied (if not already done)
2. `SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY` environment variable is set for RLS bypass
3. Test with valid admin JWT tokens

  - If we re-raise an exception, use a plain `raise` statement to keep and propagate the stack trace, and use `logger.error()` so that the stack trace is not printed in this layer (to avoid duplicate log)
  - If we do not re-raise the exception and is only logging the exception, always use `logger.exception()` (which is an equivalence  of `logger.error(exc_info=True))`
- Added the pattern above to Cursor rules to let code generated by agent follow the convention
- Added the pattern above to `.coderabbit.yaml` so this pattern is always checked at the coderabbit review

Closes AIQ-1058

body:
This PR implements a complete telemetry overlay application that accepts video files and FIT files to overlay fitness metrics onto video recordings at appropriate timestamps.

## Features Implemented

**Core Functionality:**
- Accepts multiple video formats (MP4, AVI, MOV, MKV, WMV)
- Parses FIT files to extract telemetry data
- Overlays metrics synchronized with video timeline
- Supports heart rate (bpm), speed (km/h), pace (min/km), and power (W) metrics

**User Interfaces:**
- **GUI Application** (`main.py`) - Full-featured interface with file selection, preview, and progress tracking
- **Command Line Interface** (`cli.py`) - For batch processing and automation
- **Demo Script** (`demo.py`) - Generates sample data to demonstrate functionality

**Smart Features:**
- Automatic activity type detection (cycling vs running) based on speed patterns
- Time synchronization between video frames and telemetry timestamps
- Semi-transparent overlay with color-coded metrics for optimal visibility
- Preview functionality to verify overlay before full processing
- Comprehensive error handling and progress reporting

## Technical Implementation

The application uses a modular architecture with separate components for:
- **FIT Parser** (`telemetry_overlay/fit_parser.py`) - Extracts telemetry data from FIT files
- **Video Overlay** (`telemetry_overlay/video_overlay.py`) - Handles video processing and overlay rendering
- **GUI Application** (`telemetry_overlay/app.py`) - User interface with tkinter

The overlay appears in the top-left corner with format:
```
Time: 05:23
HR: 142 bpm
Speed: 32.5 km/h
Power: 245 W
```

## Usage Examples

**GUI Mode:**
```bash
python3 main.py
```

**Command Line:**
```bash
python3 cli.py input_video.mp4 activity.fit output_with_overlay.mp4
```

**Demo with Sample Data:**
```bash
python3 demo.py
```

## Dependencies

Uses system packages for better compatibility:
- OpenCV for video processing
- pandas/numpy for data manipulation
- tkinter for GUI (Python standard library)
- Optional: fitparse for real FIT file parsing (demo works with mock data)

The implementation successfully addresses all requirements from the problem statement, providing a production-ready solution for overlaying fitness telemetry data onto video recordings.

body:
Addresses the core issue where "Copilot seems to have trouble using the tools quite often" by implementing comprehensive usability improvements that reduce friction and provide clear workflow guidance.

## Problem Statement

LLMs frequently struggled with the memory MCP tools due to:
- Failed operations when trying to add observations to non-existent entities
- Lack of clear workflow guidance (should view graph first, then create entities, then add observations)
- Confusing error messages without helpful examples
- Missing guidance on tool usage sequence

## Key Improvements

### 🔄 Auto-Creation Features
- **`add_observation`**: Now automatically creates missing entities with configurable `entityType` (defaults to "Unknown")
- **`create_relations`**: Automatically creates missing entities referenced in relationships
- **`create_entities`**: Auto-creates empty observations arrays when missing

Example - this now works even if "John" doesn't exist:
```text
#memory-test_add_observation workspaceId="project" entityName="John" observation="Software developer" entityType="Person"
```

### 📋 Enhanced Tool Descriptions & Workflow Guidance
- **`read_graph`**: Marked as "RECOMMENDED FIRST STEP" with clear guidance
- All tools now include workflow hints about when to use them
- Parameter descriptions include examples and expected formats
- Tools guide users through proper sequence: read → search → create → relate → observe

### ⚡ Improved Error Messages & Validation
- Specific error messages with corrective examples
- Better parameter validation with helpful guidance
- Auto-handling of edge cases to reduce friction

Before:
```
Error: Entity 'Alice' not found
```

After:
```
Error: entityName and observation are required. Please provide both parameters.
Example: {"entityName": "Alice", "observation": "Software engineer", "entityType": "Person"}
```

### 📚 Updated Documentation
- README now shows recommended workflow sequence with step-by-step examples
- Clear feature summary highlighting auto-creation capabilities
- Better examples demonstrating proper tool usage order

## Impact

These changes significantly improve LLM usability by:
1. **Reducing failed operations** - Auto-creation handles missing dependencies
2. **Providing clear guidance** - Tools now guide proper workflow sequence  
3. **Better error recovery** - Helpful messages show how to fix issues
4. **Lowering complexity** - Common edge cases handled automatically

The tools should now be much more intuitive and reliable for AI assistants to use correctly.

author: kirkdiggler
body:
## Summary

This PR consolidates the v2 validator improvements into the main validator, simplifying the validation system and removing all v2 references. The project is in alpha and doesn't need migration paths - we're choosing one approach and sticking with it.

## Key Changes

### 🎯 Simplified Severity System (3 levels instead of 4)
- **ERROR**: Invalid choices that block saving the draft
- **INCOMPLETE**: Missing required choices (can save, can't finalize)  
- **WARNING**: Valid but wasted choices (e.g., duplicate skills from different sources)

*Removed the Info severity level as it was redundant with Warning*

### ✨ Enhanced Validation Features
- **TypedSubmissions**: Track source of each choice (class/race/background/etc)
- **ValidationContext**: Smart prerequisite checking (e.g., expertise requires proficiency)
- **Cross-source duplicate detection**: Warn when skills are duplicated across sources
- **Deduplication logic**: Prevent redundant warnings for within-source duplicates

### 🔌 Data-Driven API Integration
- **LoadDraftFromData**: Validates class/race/background are valid constants at load time
- **Draft.ValidateChoices()**: Direct integration with choices validation using typed constants
- **Converter functions**: Handle shared→choices type conversion cleanly
- **Proper severity handling**: Missing choices are Incomplete (can save), invalid choices are Errors (can't save)

### 📝 Improved Documentation
- Updated README with actual implementation status
- Added comprehensive example tests demonstrating validation patterns
- Clear severity level definitions with real use cases

## Server Integration Pattern

The game server can now work with pure data while the toolkit maintains type safety:

```go
// Server loads draft data from DB - strings become typed constants
data := DraftData{
    ClassChoice: ClassChoice{
        ClassID: "fighter",  // Becomes classes.Fighter
    },
    RaceChoice: RaceChoice{
        RaceID: "half-elf",  // Becomes races.HalfElf
    },
}

// LoadDraftFromData validates the strings are valid
draft, err := LoadDraftFromData(data)
if err != nil {
    // Invalid class/race/background - fail fast
    return err
}

// Draft now has typed constants, can validate choices directly
result, err := draft.ValidateChoices()
if !result.CanSave {
    // Invalid choices
} else if !result.CanFinalize {
    // Missing required choices
}
```

## Testing

All tests pass with the new consolidated system:
- Added equipment choices to Wizard and Fighter tests
- Fixed duplicate warning logic to avoid redundant messages
- Example tests demonstrate various validation scenarios
- Integration tests verify Draft↔choices package interaction

## Breaking Changes

- Removed Info severity level (merged into Warning)
- Changed validation function signatures to use new types
- No v2 references remain - single clean implementation
- Missing choices now return Incomplete severity (not Error)

## Next Steps

Draft integration with rpg-api will be a separate PR, allowing us to:
1. Focus on getting the validation system right first
2. Integrate with rpg-api character draft system cleanly
3. Keep changes focused and reviewable
